sentences.text: (a) Serial number of the case : 1387-2024 (b) Name of the complainant : Delhi Administration/Food  Inspector, Department of PFA (c) Name of the accused person : Mudassar Ansari s/o  Sh Dada Mallick Ansari  r/o 392, Sector-7, R K  Puram, New Delhi-22.
(d) Offences charged of : Section 16 of PFA Act.

(e) Plea of the accused : Pleaded not guilty (f) Final Judgment : Accused stands  acquitted.
(g) Date of institution of case : 18.10.2010 (h) Date of final arguments : 07.05.2024 (i) Date of Judgment : 27.05.2024
BRIEF FACTS OF THE CASE 1.

The present is a complaint filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (herein after referred to as Cr. Case 1387-2024 Delhi Administration Vs.. Mudassar Ansari Page No.
1 of 8 PFA Act), alleging that the accused has violated the provisions of Section 2 (ia) (a) & (m) of the PFA Act.

sentences.text: 2. Initially, after conclusion of the trial, the accused was convicted by the then, Ld. ACMM vide order dated 29.04.2017 under section 16(1)(a) of the PFA act read with section 7 of the PFA act and was accordingly sentenced.
3. The accused had challenged the order before the appellate court.

The Ld. ASJ-04 had set aside the order of conviction and sentence vide order dated 09.05.2023 and remanded back the case with the following observations:

1 "... 26.
On 15.02.2023, the following questio was framed by me:

The neat question that arises in the present case is whether test conducted by the PA as well as CFL was in accordance with the notification issued by the Government in this regard, since the name of method of analysis is different in PA report from the one mentioned in the CFL report.
27.

In my view,after hearing the counsel appearing, it seems that the said question is a mixed question of law and facts and what the PA or official from CFL is going to tell the court would itself be a matter of evidence.

28. Therefore, in these circumstances, the matter deserve to be remanded back to the Ld ACMM as this issue is central to the facts in issue and needs to be determined before the guilt of the accused can be established..."
4.
Accordingly, despite opportunity, the prosecution did not lead any evidence as well as the accused.
Therefore, final arguments were heard afresh at length on behalf of the accused and the department.
Cr. Case 1387-2024 Delhi Administration Vs.. Mudassar Ansari Page No. 2 of 8 5.

sentences.text: During the course of arguments, the accused did not dispute the proceedings conducted by the department regarding the lifting of the sample or the subsequent proceedings.
The counsel for the accused has centered his arguments primarily on the ground that the sample in question which was examined by the CFL was not representative in character.
He has emphatically argued that the sample in question was Paneer and it is a perishable item and subject to decay.

He has relied upon several judgments in support of his contentions as well as the Journal, which was examined in the testimony of DW-1 and CW-1, to show that even if the Paneer is well preserved with addition of 0.4%
formalin, the sample stored for a period of 7, 14 and 21 days will witness decrease in the fat present in the Paneer and if the Paneer is analysised after 21 days, the decrease will be at an average of 7.1%
and thus, the fat percentage found by the CFL to be around 46% was the result of deterioration of the sample and it amply shows that the fat percentage at the time of lifting of the sample would have been more than 50% ie the minimum standard.
Secondly, the prosecution has failed to show the method of analysis were the same as notified by the department.

6. On the other hand, Ld. SPP contended that the report of CFL is conclusive in nature and replaces the report of the PA and has categorically shown that the fat percentage was less then the minimum standard and it cannot be brush aside merely on the basis of research paper, which is Ex.DW1/A and all the parameters as per the Cr. Case 1387-2024 Delhi Administration Vs..
Mudassar Ansari Page No. 3 of 8 Regulations have been followed to prepare the report and no contradictions could be brought on record qua the same.
7. Before proceeding further, it is pertinent to refer to the facts of the case and the evidence available on record.

2 8.

It is the case of the department that on 21.07.2010, the Food Official consisting of Food Inspector Gian Chand and Field Assistant Satish Gaur under the supervision of SDM/LHA Vivek Kumar Tripathi along with staff reached at the premises of M/s Lazeem Sweets Shop No. 8, Sector-5, R K Puram, New Delhi and found the vendor conducting the business of various food articles, which were lying stored/exposed for sale of human consumption.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Thereafter, 750 grams of 'Paneer' was purchased as a sample from the vendor, which was lying in open tray bearing No Label or declaration and then as per the rules, was divided into three parts.
9. Further, the one sample was sent to the public analyst intact condition and other two counter parts were deposited with SDM/LHA.

Thereafter, the Food Analyst vide its report dated 18.08.2010,
found that the sample was not confirming to the standards prescribed on the ground that the percentage of the milk fat was less then the prescribed minimum limit of 50%.

Then, upon the receipt of the report, investigation was directed which was carried out by the FI and after Cr. Case 1387-2024 Delhi Administration Vs.. Mudassar Ansari Page No. 4 of 8 obtaining sanction u/s 20 of the PFA Act, the complaint was filed in the court.
10.

sentences.text:
Further, the accused was summoned after taking cognizance and he preferred an application under section 13 (2) of the PFA Act and the second counter part of the sample was selected by the accused, which was sent to the Central Food Laboratory and the Director analyzed the sample and gave a report vide Certificate dated 14.12.2010, opining that the sample does not confirm to the standards.
11.

Accordingly, notice was framed against the accused for the offence punishable u/s 7/16 (1) (a) of the PFA Act for the violation of section 2 (ia) (a) & (m).
12.
Thereafter, prosecution evidence was recorded, during which the prosecution examined three witnesses.
Then, statement of the accused was recorded and accused has led the defence evidence.
Furthermore, final arguments were heard and accused was initially convicted.
As per the directions of Ld Sessions Court, the final arguments have been heard again at length and the matter was reserved for orders.

13. After going through the material on record, I am of the opinion that the prosecution has proved the lifting of the sample proceedings beyond reasonable doubt and the accused could not bring on record Cr. Case 1387-2024 Delhi Administration Vs.. Mudassar Ansari Page No. 5 of 8 any material contradiction qua the testimony of PW-1, PW-2 and PW- 3 qua the same.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Now the question which is to be analyzed is whether the test conducted by the sample was in accordance with the notification issued by the Government and whether the method of analysis were different in the report of the PA or the Director, CFL.

After hearing the arguments and the judgments relied upon by the parties, I am of the opinion that the report of the PA stands replaced upon the certificate issued by the Director, CFL and thus, the method adopted by the PA need not to be looked into.
However, it is pertinent to observe that the prosecution,did not examine the Director, CFL despite opportunity to establish that the method used was a notified method by the Government.
Further, the prosecution did not point out the rules and regulations to show that the method adopted by the Director, CFL was falling within the notified methods.

Da vs Mudassar Ansari on 27 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43401717/
3 14.

Even if, it is presumed that the method adopted was a notified method, the next question which arises for analysis is whether the sample on the date of the examination was fit for analysis and there was no deterioration to the said effect.
The prosecution has contended that the report of the Director, CFL is conclusive in nature and thus, there is no doubt that the sample was not fit for analysis.

However, at this stage, reliance has to be placed upon the testimony of DW-2, who was the Principal Scientist, NDRI, who was examined u/s 311 Cr.P.C and has relied upon a Journal, which is Ex.DW1/A and he has referred Cr. Case 1387-2024 Delhi Administration Vs..

Mudassar Ansari Page No. 6 of 8 to the research paper mentioning that the sample of Paneer, if preserved with addition of 0.4% formalin and stored for a period of 21 days, decreased of an average of 7.1% in the fat percentage of the original fat will be seen.

The counsel for the accused in order to support the reasoning mentioned in the research paper had referred the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in case titled as State vs Suresh Chand (Crl No. 80/2009) wherein it has been observed that if a sample of Paneer is analyzed after a period of four months, the essential rights of the accused u/s 13 (2) of the Act will be frustrated and the de-composition will be noticed.
15.

In the present case also, the complaint was filed after a period of three months and the sample was analyzed by the Director, CFL after almost five months, which indicates that the sample would have lost its representative character and the prosecution has not brought on record any evidence to rebut the claim of the accused by proving that the sample of Paneer never lost its original form, even when it was examined by the Director, CFL.
On the other hand, in the report of the CFL, it could be noticed that the colour of the sample Paneer was off white indicating deterioration.

Thus, as on date,
there are two possible views, one indicating to the guilt of the accused on the basis of the report of the Director of CFL and another to the innocense of the accused, wherein it has come on record as a probable consequence that the sample of Paneer has lost its original form and decreased in Cr. Case 1387-2024 Delhi Administration Vs..
Mudassar Ansari Page No. 7 of 8 the original fat of the sample was possible.
It is an established principle that in case of two possible views, the one favouring the accused has to be taken.

Thus, in the present case, there is a possibility that the sample of Paneer when examined by the Director, CFL was not representative in character and decrease in the fat percentage was also possible and thus, there is a doubt that the sample on the date of lifting was having percentage more than 50% and it has lost the fat percentage on account of the lapse of time,
when the sample was analyzed.
16.
In view of the above discussion, I am of the opinion that the prosecution has failed to establish its case against the accused beyond reasonable doubt.
Accordingly, accused Mudassar Ansari, stands acquitted for offence under Section 16 of PFA Act.
17. Accused is directed to furnish personal bonds U/s 437A Cr.PC in the sum of Rs.10,000/-.
Announced in the open Court on 27th May, 2024 This judgment contains eight pages and each page is signed by me.
ABHISHEK KUMAR Date: 2024.05.28 15:15:47 +0530 (ABHISHEK KUMAR) ACMM-01/NEW DELHI DISTRICT PATIALA HOUSE COURTS/NEW DELHI 27.05.2024
